levels.text: Secondary coverage is not optional.
"Secondary coverage is not optional. If the external record is missing we hold the claim for a human, we never auto-deny." - clinical operations lead, 2026-09-17.

INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT (EXCERPT) - Clinical operations lead, Northstar Health, 2026-09-17

Q: What happens today when a claim includes secondary coverage?
A: Secondary coverage is not optional. If the external record is missing we hold the claim for a human, we never auto-deny.

Q: How often is the external record missing?
A: Often enough to matter. The provider has no availability commitment; outages happen monthly.

Q: What should automation do in that case?
A: Hold and route to review. Speed matters, but a wrong denial costs more than a delay.
When secondary coverage is present, the workflow calls lookupSecondaryCoverage(external: true) and waits for the record before deciding.

The customer workflow has two branches. The primary branch is fully internal. The secondary branch calls an external record lookup and blocks until it answers; if the record is absent the claim is held for human review.

Customer workflow - intake through decision

Step 1. Claim arrives with structured coverage fields.

Step 2. Primary coverage validated against the internal policy engine (sub-second).

Step 3. When secondary coverage is present, the workflow calls lookupSecondaryCoverage(external: true) and waits for the record before deciding. The provider is called synchronously; there is no timeout branch.

Step 4. If the record is present, auto-adjudicate. If the record is absent, hold the claim for human review. The hold queue is reviewed within one business day.

Step 5. Decision and evidence are written to the claim record.
The secondary branch is real and synchronous.
Observed 14 claims end to end. 9 used the primary branch only; 5 included secondary coverage and all 5 waited on the external lookup (median 1.8 s, max 41 s).

WORKFLOW OBSERVATION - 2026-09-19, Northstar claims intake (shadow session)

Method: passive observation of 14 consecutive claims with operations staff.

Primary branch: 9/14 claims, fully internal, median 0.6 s to decision.
Secondary branch: 5/14 claims. Each called the external record lookup synchronously.
  Lookup latency: median 1.8 s, p95 12 s, max 41 s.
  Record present: 4/5. Record ABSENT: 1/5 - claim held for human review, resolved next morning.

Interview cross-check: staff confirmed the hold path is correct behavior, not an error.
Implication: automation must treat an absent record as a hold condition, never a denial.

No availability commitment exists.
GET /records/{coverageId} returns 200 with the record, 404 when absent, 503 during provider outages. The contract documents no uptime commitment and no timeout guarantee.

External record API - provider contract (excerpt)

GET /records/{coverageId}

  • 200 - record present (JSON body, see schema)
  • 404 - record absent; absence is a valid steady state, not an error
  • 503 - provider outage; observed monthly, duration minutes to hours

Availability: no uptime commitment is documented. No timeout guarantee is documented. Consumers must tolerate indefinite absence.

Rate limits: 10 rps per client key. Auth: client certificate, rotated quarterly.
